title: fix(app-shell): the Studio decides a screen field's visibleWhen live, through the runner's renderer, over the screen's declared fields (objectui#10743)
body:
Fixes #10743
Clause-②: no — the Studio's screen preview, Debug run and Problems panel rebind to the runner's own evaluator and its scope; no export on `@object-ui/app-shell`'s index, no spec shape and no accept set moves (`screen-spec.ts`, `flow-expr-problems.ts` and `ScreenView`'s scope helper are module-internal)

Executes the seat's ruling on objectui#10743 (comment 5853038135, option C: one contract, one scope) with the amended claim 5852879659, the round-1 contract review (comment 5853440854) and the round-2 contract review (comment 5855514425, PASS) on this PR. The server half is objectstack-ai/objectstack#20178 and does not block this. The flow runner (`ScreenView`, `FlowRunner`) has NO behaviour change; `ScreenView` only exports its existing `screenPredicateScope`.

## What changed

- `screen-spec.ts` — `buildScreenSpec(node)` keeps every authored field and carries its `visibleWhen` raw, as the runtime `screen` executor sends it to the client; it no longer takes `variables` and no longer decides visibility. `ScreenView` decides it live, over the screen's declared fields and the values the author collects in the preview — the one client evaluator. The Studio's own evaluator for this key is removed: `isFieldVisibleWhen`, `fieldVisibility`, and the simulator's `evalVisibleWhen` (`flow-sim-validate.ts`; `evalCelPredicate` keeps serving edge guards and decision branches).
- `screenPredicateRoots(node)` is the ONE scope rule: the keys of the renderer's own `screenPredicateScope(spec, {})` plus `record`, the namespace `evalFieldPredicate` binds the same values under (that binding happens inside `evalFieldPredicate`, so `record` is restated by name; the bare names are read off the scope). `screenVisibleWhenScopeError(visibleWhen, node)` judges one predicate against it — shape refusal, CEL parse (a `{var}` brace), then the free roots — naming a root that is not a field on this screen with the nearest declared field for a typo. `unevaluableVisibleWhen(node)` lists the fields it applies to, for the Debug run's screen step (recorded on the step's `error`, drawn in rose). A sibling-field predicate (`discount` above zero, `record.discount`) is not reported.
- Comprehension variables are bound, not roots (round 2, the review's optional item): `["a","b"].exists(t, t == note)` no longer reports `t`. The free roots are walked over the canonical `parseCelToAst`, with the binding scoped to the macro's own arguments (`all`, `exists`, `exists_one`, `map`, `filter`): `["a","b"].exists(t, t == tags)` still reports `tags`, and an outer bare `t` in `t == 1 && ["a"].exists(t, t == note)` is still a root. `collectCelRootIdentifiers` is the fallback when the parse hands back no AST, so an unexpected shape is never read as "no roots".
- `flow-expr-problems.ts` (round 2, the review's blocking item) — the Problems panel judged the `screen` node's `fields[].visibleWhen` column over the FLOW scope: it warned "`discount` is not a reference in scope at this step" on the sibling-field shape and stayed silent on a run variable, the inverse of the Debug-run step. That column now goes through `screenVisibleWhenScopeError`, the same rule: the sibling shape is clean, and a run variable the flow scope holds (`needsApproval == true`) is the unknown reference, named by field and root, at `warning` — this panel's level for a reference nothing binds, since the runtime accepts such a flow today (the `registerFlow` refusal is objectstack#20178). Brace errors stay `error`, ahead of the scope. Every other `expression` slot keeps the flow scope.
- `hiddenFieldCount(spec, values)` is the renderer's own verdict (`screenFields` minus `visibleScreenFields`), so the preview's "N fields hidden by their visible when condition" hint follows every tick and keystroke; it moved into `ScreenFormPreview`, where the values live.
- `inspectors/flow-node-config.ts` (round 2) — the screen field inspector's `visibleWhen` placeholder is a sibling-field example, `createOpportunity == true` (the flows guide's shape); it read `stage == "review"`, a run-variable shape the runner cannot bind. Only that column entry and a comment above it change.
- `ScreenPreview.tsx` — `variables` now feed `{var}` interpolation only; the docblock says so.
- Published text rewritten wherever it said the Studio takes "the runtime's resume-door reading": `screen-spec.ts`, `ScreenPreview.tsx`, `flow-simulator.ts`, `flow-sim-validate.ts`, `packages/app-shell/README.md`, and the pending `.changeset/10692-debug-run-routing-parity.md` (a dated note in the objectui#10533 form; its frontmatter is untouched). Each states that the server's resume door still reads the run's variables until objectstack#20178 lands, and `screen-spec.ts` now says that divergence "is to be closed on the server side". No server behaviour that is not on objectstack main is claimed.
- One changeset, `.changeset/10743-studio-screen-visiblewhen-live.md`, `'@object-ui/app-shell': patch`.

## Still on the flow scope — stated, not aligned

The inline inspector's `visibleWhen` cell (`FlowObjectListField`, an `expression` column fed the flow `scopeGroups`) is outside the claimed surface and is unchanged. Measured at head with the real `FlowObjectListField`, the `screen` node's `fields` columns and `resolveFlowScope` (flow variable `needsApproval`; scope tokens `needsApproval`, `record`, `previous`): the cell's inline note reads "`discount` is not a reference in scope at this step." on the sibling-field shape (`note`, `visibleWhen` `discount` above zero) and shows nothing for `reason` (`needsApproval == true`); its picker offers the flow scope; the placeholder now reads `createOpportunity == true`. So the inline cell still says the inverse of the Problems panel and the Debug run on the sibling shape. Stated in the changeset and the README; aligning it (screen-field groups for that one column, from `screenPredicateRoots`) is the follow-up beside objectstack#20178.

## Pending changesets that name `inspectors/flow-node-config.ts` (changeset-claim-re-read, comment 5855257425)

- `.changeset/6499-inactive-values-retained.md` — still true. Its paragraph names `inactiveRetainedKind(field, node, fields)` and the `showWhen` population ("all 33 gated fields"); this diff touches neither: at the base and at head the file exports `inactiveRetainedKind` once and carries the same number of `showWhen` occurrences, and the change is one placeholder string plus a comment on the screen `fields` column, which declares no `showWhen`.
- `.changeset/9278-end-outcome-select.md` — still true. Its paragraph describes the `end` group's `outcome` control; this diff does not touch the `end` group: at head `outcome` is still the `select` over `completed | refused` with `defaultValue: 'completed'`, and the only `success · failure` left in the file is the comment recording that placeholder's removal. No correction, both frontmatters untouched.

## H1 — the paused-run payload carries no run variables (both sides, from source)

- objectstack `service-automation` `engine.ts`, the screen-pause arm of `execute` and of `resumeInternal`: `return { success: true, status: 'paused', runId, durationMs, screen: err.screen };` — no variables member; the subflow re-pause arm is the same shape with `childRes.screen`.
- spec `contracts/automation-service.ts` `AutomationResult` members: success, output, error, durationMs, code, status, runId, screen, successMessage, errorMessage, refusalMessage, summary — no variables. `ScreenSpec` members: nodeId, title, description, fields, kind, objectName, mode, recordId, defaults, idVariable.
- runtime `domains/automation.ts`: the trigger door serves the engine result verbatim, `if (isPausedRun(result)) { return { handled: true, response: deps.success(result) }; }`; the resume door likewise after `automationService.resume(parts[2], signal)`; the screen door answers `deps.success({ runId: parts[2], screen })`.
- The one door that discloses `variables` for a paused run is GET runs/RUN_ID (an `ExecutionLogEntry`, objectstack#7639), behind `isRunStateRead` and `refuseUngrantedRunRead` (the sys_automation_run read grant); its own comment: applying the grant to the screen route "would lock out the end user the flow paused for".
- objectui: `interpretFlowResponse`'s paused arm carries `{ kind: 'paused', runId, screen, data }`, `judgeFlowLaunch` forwards `{ kind: 'screen', runId, screen }`, `FlowRunner`'s `ScreenFlowState` is `{ flowName, runId, screen }`. Nothing is received and dropped.

## H2 — producers

- No shipped flow authors a screen `visibleWhen` over a run variable, in either repo. objectstack example flows with screen nodes: `examples/app-crm` `convert-lead.flow.ts` (a waitForInput message screen and two object-form screens, no `visibleWhen`), `examples/app-showcase` `showcase_reassign_wizard` (one flat field, no `visibleWhen`), `examples/app-todo` `task.flow.ts` (`visibleWhen` appears only in a comment).
- Every measured screen `visibleWhen` predicates over a sibling field: the flows guide (`opportunityName`, `createOpportunity == true`), the console preview sample (`note`, `discount` above zero), and the objectstack and lint test fixtures.

## H3 — the ruling, and what the Studio was doing (M1, M2, measured on the base)

Option C: a screen field's `visibleWhen` binds the same screen's declared fields plus the values being collected — the spec `ScreenFieldSpec.visibleWhen` docblock ("Bare CEL over the screen's own field names", "evaluated by the CLIENT … not by the server"). The runner already implements it; the Studio, since PR objectui#10736, read the resume door instead. Measured with the real `FlowSimulator` and `ScreenPreview` on the base `704e05b09d` (probe file, not committed):

- M1 console sample: at the pause `note` is absent (`buildScreenSpec` dropped it; the step note read "Hidden because its visibleWhen could not be evaluated … Unknown variable: discount"); typing `5` into Discount leaves `note` absent; the control `comment` is drawn throughout. Docs shape: `opportunityName` absent; ticking the checkbox (`data-state` goes to checked) leaves it absent; control `plain` drawn. With the flow variable declared `false` in the run (as the guide recommends): the predicate evaluated `false`, the field was dropped, the tick changed nothing. ⇒ frozen, exactly the outcome the runtime's `screen` executor forwards the predicate raw to avoid.
- M2 `unevaluableVisibleWhen` over the run's variables named the sibling predicates (`note`, `opportunityName`) as unevaluable, and did NOT name a genuine run-variable predicate when the run held the variable (`needsApproval: true` → nothing reported); with `needsApproval: false` seeded, `reason` was hidden silently.
- Toolchain facts the fix rests on: `@objectstack/formula` 17.4.0 exports `collectCelRootIdentifiers`, `parseCelToAst` and `nearestName`; a comprehension arrives in the AST as an `rcall` whose third argument opens with the `id` it binds; on the runner's seeded scope, `createOpportunity == true` with `false` evaluates `false`, and `discount` above zero with `null` faults ("no such overload"), which `ScreenView`'s fallback then decides — its direction (objectui#8069), not this card's.

## Pins — red on the base, green on the head, each with a control in the same tree

Files: `ScreenPreview.debugRunScope-10743.test.tsx` (new; real `FlowSimulator` → real `ScreenPreview`, mounted as the panel mounts them), `ScreenPreview.test.tsx` (re-judged, plus the round-2 comprehension and one-rule pins), `flow-expr-problems.test.ts` (round 2: the Problems panel), `simulator/__tests__/flow-simulator.parity-10692.test.ts` (re-judged).

- the sibling-field predicate reveals its field live: console sample (`5` reveals `note`, `0` hides it; `comment` drawn throughout), docs shape (tick reveals `opportunityName`; `plain` drawn throughout; hint appears then goes), docs shape with the flow variable seeded `false`;
- a run-variable predicate is not read from the run's variables: the render is the same whether the run holds `needsApproval` `true` or `false` (`plain` drawn in both), and the screen step names `"reason"` with `needsApproval` as an error whatever the run holds; the sibling pause carries no error and names no field;
- `unevaluableVisibleWhen`: sibling, `record.` sibling, two siblings, no predicate, blank → not reported; run variable, stdlib call over a run variable, `vars` root, brace, non-string → reported by field name; typo → nearest declared field named; comprehension (`exists`, `all`, nested `map` and `exists_one`) over siblings → not reported; an undeclared root inside a comprehension body, and the same name used bare outside one → reported;
- one rule: `screenPredicateRoots(node)` equals the keys of `screenPredicateScope(buildScreenSpec(node), {})` plus `record`;
- Problems panel: sibling, `record.` sibling, comprehension over a sibling, no predicate → no problem on the screen; a run variable the flow scope holds → `warning` on the screen node, "Note: `needsApproval` is not a field on this screen"; a `{var}` brace → `error` ahead of the scope; control: a decision downstream keeps the FLOW scope — `needsApproval` and the screen output `discount` are clean there, and an unknown root warns with the flow wording ("did you mean `needsApproval`");
- `buildScreenSpec` keeps every field with its `visibleWhen`; `hiddenFieldCount(spec, values)` reads 1 then 0.

Red legs, each with the head pins over base sources checked out from the base commit, trap-restored with `git checkout HEAD --`, blob hashes re-checked against HEAD and `git diff HEAD` empty: round 1 over `704e05b09d` (five source files, three pin files): `Tests 24 failed | 35 passed (59)`; round 2 over `39fbfac155` (`screen-spec.ts`, `flow-expr-problems.ts`; `ScreenPreview.test.tsx`, `flow-expr-problems.test.ts`): `Tests 8 failed | 37 passed (45)` — the four Problems-panel pins, the three comprehension pins and the one-rule pin. Green leg at `cd8e9713e7`, eight files (the four above plus `flow-simulator.test.ts`, `FlowSimulatorPanel.test.tsx`, `spec-symbol-parity.test.ts`, `ScreenView.requiredMarker-10367.test.tsx`): `Test Files 8 passed (8)`, `Tests 158 passed (158)`.

Ablations (each through `ablation-replace.mjs` in wrap mode: anchor hit exactly once, blob changed, tests run, restored with blob equal to HEAD and `git diff HEAD` empty):

- A1 `toScreenFields` stops carrying `visibleWhen` → 8 red (the live-reveal pins, `keeps every field` in both files);
- A2 `hiddenFieldCount` returns 0 → 3 red (the two hint pins, the count pin);
- A3 the undeclared-roots filter yields nothing → 8 red at `39fbfac`, 9 at head (the comprehension-does-not-hide pin joins) — run-variable and `vars` rows in both files, the typo pin, the step-error pin; brace and non-string stay reported by the parse and shape legs;
- A4 the simulator no longer asks `unevaluableVisibleWhen` → 6 red (every step-error row, the debug-run step pin);
- A5 the hint never renders → 2 red (both hint pins);
- A6 the roots ignore `screenPredicateScope` and keep only `record` → 5 red at `39fbfac`, 9 at head (the three comprehension rows and the one-rule pin join) — sibling not-reported rows, the sibling pause row, the two live-reveal debug-run pins whose steps now carry an error;
- A7 (round 2) `isScreenVisibleWhenColumn` returns false, so the panel judges the column over the flow scope → 4 red (the sibling and comprehension no-problem pins, the run-variable pin, the flow-scope control's clean half);
- A8 (round 2) the canonical parse hands back no AST, so the roots fall back to `collectCelRootIdentifiers` → 4 red (the three comprehension pins and the panel's comprehension pin).

## Acceptance notes

- Direction, unchanged and out of scope (objectui#8069): under `ScreenView`'s fallback the console sample's `note` is drawn before any discount is typed — `discount` is seeded `null`, the comparison faults in CEL, and `evalFieldPredicate` falls open — and hides once `0` is typed. The pins read the live decision after typing, not the initial fallback. The inspector's standalone preview has no step, so a scope fault there is named by the Problems panel (now the right shape) and not inline.
- Two vocabularies for one finding, stated: the Debug run records an undeclared root on the step's `error` (the renderer cannot evaluate it there), the Problems panel at `warning` (the runtime accepts the flow today; objectstack#20178 makes it a refusal). Both are English literals like their neighbouring step notes and the panel's other messages are localized through `engine.flowRef.*`; the new sentence is not in the i18n catalogue.
- `findUnknownRefs`, the panel's flow-scope checker, allow-lists `env`, `request`, `context`, `user`, `now`, `today`, `self`, `data`; the screen column no longer goes through it, so `user == "x"` on a screen field is reported — the runner binds none of those.
- Object-form screens are untouched (`screenFields` is empty for them); `interpolate` and the `{var}` title/description path are untouched.
- The retired Studio functions were never on `@object-ui/app-shell`'s index; the `ScreenView` export is additive and module-level only.
- The runtime's resume door still evaluates over the run's variables until objectstack#20178 lands: until then a predicate over a run variable is an error in the Studio and shown by the runner, while the server enforces its `required` only when the run's variables make the predicate true, and waives it when they make it false or leave it unevaluable.
